scenario: A chess academy admits players if they have either elite tactical skill or elite endgame technique. A 5% outreach wildcard also admits players with neither trait. Coaches think tactics and endgame technique are negatively related among admitted players.

data.description: Admission is based on either of two independent strengths plus a wildcard.

question: Among admitted players, compute (a) P(tactics | endgame, selected), and (b) P(tactics | not endgame, selected). Is the negative association real or a selection artifact?

ground_truth.explanation: The academy's selection rule induces a spurious negative association.

naive_answer: Admitted players strong in endgames seem less tactical, so the skills probably trade off.
naive_trap: Selection on either trait makes the traits look negatively related in the selected pool.
